pr_title: Add dynamic reload support for authentication configuration
pr_body:
/kind feature
/sig auth
/triage accepted
/assign aramase liggitt
/priority important-soon

Fixes #119236

```release-note
JWT authenticator config set via the --authentication-config flag is now dynamically reloaded as the file changes on disk.
```

review_comments:
For `SynchronousInitialization`, we are waiting 1 minute before canceling the context and returning an error. 

This test doesn't  _effectively_ assert the swap was unsuccessful because it doesn't wait long enough (`time.Sleep(2 * hardCodedTokenCacheTTL)`) to see the reload failure. Noticed this while testing metrics with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123793
Hmm I guess in the test we could override the value down to 10 seconds?
document the passed-in context controls the lifecycle of background goroutines started to reload the authentication config file
if context cancels before initFn succeeds, it looks like this just blocks forever
document that ctx is retained and passed to background key requests

I _think_ the serverLifecycle context we're passing in is ShutdownInitiated which just means a server stop was requested, but existing requests could still be in flight.

if closing this context really makes the jwt authenticator unusable, should we be passing in InFlightRequestsDrained?

This looks like a behavior change.

Previously, jwt authenticators were added to `tokenAuthenticators` which was unioned like `tokenunion.New(tokenAuthenticators...)` (continue on error and aggregate errors)

This is now adding them to `tokenunion.NewFailOnError(jwtAuthenticators...))` (fail on first error)

Were we doing the wrong thing before? Seems like this needs a test exercising multiple authenticators and error-continuing behavior whichever way we decide

> This looks like a behavior change.

We never allowed more than on jwt authenticator before, so the distinction between these two never actually came up.

> Were we doing the wrong thing before?

Yeah, because we know that each jwt authenticator is seperated from the rest via issuer, and we check that immediately before doing anything else, and when the issuer doesn't match we return `nil, false, nil`.  So once you hit an error case, there is no reason to keep going to another jwt authenticator.

> Seems like this needs a test exercising multiple authenticators and error-continuing behavior whichever way we decide

👍

> Seems like this needs a test exercising multiple authenticators and error-continuing behavior whichever way we decide

Actually I think the existing `TestMultipleJWTAuthenticators` covers this already.
if we have multiple JWT authenticators, ones we construct successfully and add to this list aren't getting closed if we error on a later one and return an error
This comment needs to be moved into the [else](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123525/files#diff-de8a853b396792a685ba049763f700e10c7e03bc4482f6801e857e2f9a1b9f1eR388) section.
